newsitem.title: USA: Time Warner uses Zenith analog set-tops.
newsitem.headline: Time Warner uses Zenith analog set-tops.

text.p: Zenith Electronics Corp said Time Warner Cable, a unit of Time Warner Inc, is expanding channel offerings and services in Texas with 750-megahertz versions of Zenith's analog set-top box.

It said the 285,000-subscriber system in San Antonio, Texas, is using Zenith's MM2500 devices to increase its capacity to 117 channels and is expanding its interactive capabilities for opinion polling, system status monitoring and impulse pay-per-view.
Time Warner also plans to bring real-time two-way capability to its subscribers in San Diego, Calif.
In San Diego, Time Warner's system serves about 180,000 subscribers. It will use Zenith's MM2500 addressable set-tops starting in the spring.
Zenith did not disclose the value of the equipment orders.

Separately, Zenith reported a successful five-month trial of its "telco return" cable modem system involving subscribers in a Chicago-area cable system. By combining their existing telephone modem and a high-speed cable modem, the cable subscribers achieved fast access to the Internet and online services.
Trial results were announced in New Orleans at the National cable Television Association convention.

Zenith's telco-return system provides downstream access over cable systems at speeds of 4 megabits per second, and upstream access using subscribers' existing telephone modems, making it possible for one-way cable systems to offer cable modem services.
Based on the trial, cable operators are studying full-scale deployments of the telco return modem, Zenith said.
